explanation_rule: 言う becomes 申す in 謙譲語II. This form lowers the speaker's own speech without directing the humility at a specific person, making it standard for formal self-introduction.
explanation_example: 田中と申します。どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。(My name is Tanaka. I look forward to working with you.)
source: 文化審議会答申「敬語の指針」(2007) via Yamaguchi Univ. paper

english_meaning: Have you looked at / seen it?
explanation_rule: 見る becomes ご覧になる in 尊敬語. Use this honorific form when asking a superior or client whether they have seen something, to show respect for their action.
explanation_example: 資料はご覧になりましたか？(Have you had a chance to look at the materials?)

english_meaning: I will go / visit your company
explanation_rule: 行く becomes 参る in 謙譲語II. This form lowers the speaker's own movement without directing the humility at the destination, and is standard in formal written and spoken Japanese.
explanation_example: 来週月曜日に御社に参ります。(I will visit your company this coming Monday.)
source: 文化審議会答申「敬語の指針」(2007) via Yamaguchi Univ. paper

keigo_jp: 明日いらっしゃいますか
explanation_rule: 来る becomes いらっしゃる in 尊敬語. This honorific form applies when a superior or client is the one coming to a location. It also serves as the honorific for いる and 行く.
explanation_example: 明日の会議にいらっしゃいますか？(Will you be coming to the meeting tomorrow?)

explanation_rule: いる becomes おる in 謙譲語II. This form politely lowers the speaker's own state of being without directing the humility at a specific person. It is common in written business Japanese.
explanation_example: 現在、東京本社におります。(I am currently at the Tokyo headquarters.)

english_meaning: I will confirm / check on that
explanation_rule: する becomes いたす in 謙譲語II. This is one of the most frequently used humble verbs in business Japanese. It pairs naturally with the お/ご noun prefix pattern, such as ご確認いたします.
explanation_example: 後ほどご確認いたします。(I will look into that for you shortly.)

english_meaning: I am aware of it / I know
explanation_rule: 知る becomes 存じる in 謙譲語II. This form politely lowers the speaker's own knowledge. Combining it with おります adds a further layer of formality suited to email.
explanation_example: その件につきましては存じております。(I am aware of that matter.)

keigo_jp: お電話いただきました
explanation_rule: もらう becomes いただく in 謙譲語I. This directed humble form is used when receiving from a specific person of higher status. The humility is aimed at the caller. Adding お before the noun adds further respect.
explanation_example: 先ほどお電話いただきありがとうございます。(Thank you for calling me earlier.)

keigo_jp: そうおっしゃいました
explanation_rule: 言う becomes おっしゃる in 尊敬語. Use this honorific form when referring to the words of a superior or client. It is the standard choice when quoting or referencing what they said.
explanation_example: 先ほどおっしゃっていた件について確認いたします。(I will follow up on the point you raised earlier.)

explanation_rule: ある becomes ございます in 丁寧語. This is the most formal polite form of ある. It raises the overall register of the sentence without directing humility at any specific person.
explanation_example: お手元に資料がございますでしょうか？(Do you have the materials in front of you?)
